newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India sees buyers at low levels.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India sees buyers at low levels.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) saw some buying at low levels as the local market held on to its gains.
"There was some buying from States-side people yesterday which carried on today in European time," said a trader.

The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI rose 1.29 points, 2.21 percent, to 59.99 points, with the premium over the local market at 8.17 percent, after the Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index gained 88.71 points, 2.7 percent, to 3,129.69.
"The GDRs are following the local market higher," said a trader.

ITC bounced 50 cents to $10.00/$11.00 on Indian newspaper reports that Britain's B.A.T Industries aimed to increase its 31.8 percent stake in the company and had bought 700,000 shares on the local market.
B.A.T denied the reports, a spokesman telling Reuters in London, "If we were building a stake in ITC, we would not do it through the foreign investor route in the stockmarket."
Daily turnover in ITC is around 7.0 million shares on the local market.
Sentiment in India remains weak however with the index still recovering from its brush with 3,000 points.
"I think that any intelligent buyer is looking to sell in to strength in this market if it lasts much longer," said a trader.
Elswehere, the rest of Asia was firm.

The Capel Korea GDR Index ended up 2.55 points, 3.71 percent, at 71.48 points, a premium of 23.69 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index gained 12.43 points to 830.21 points on more hopes of interest rate cuts.
With Taiwan on holiday the Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.27 points at 90.78, a premium of 71.48.
